speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning; I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; to begin our evaluation, how many hours old were you when these symptoms first started?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you; given the bilious vomiting and your brother's history of pyloric stenosis, was the vomitus green or brown, and have you noticed any abdominal distension? Also, did the vomiting occur after every feeding?

text: RESULTS: The x-ray shows a 'double bubble' sign indicative of duodenal atresia.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Brother had pyloric stenosis. Social history: NA

speaker: Patient
text: Physical examination shows epicanthus, upward slanting of the eyelids, low-set ears, and a single transverse palmar crease. A grade 2/6 holosystolic murmur heard at the left mid to lower sternal border. The lungs are clear to auscultation. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.
